title: Localized ring-sheaf mates evaluated along graphs
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme, let $u:V\to B$ be an object of its small pro-étale site with the universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use the inverse image $u^{-1}$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] on abelian sheaves (and its induced ring-object functor). Let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $B_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$, respectively, and let $\beta:u^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be a ring-sheaf isomorphism. Under the restriction identification of clause (1) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], write $\bar\beta:R|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}S$; restriction and its ring operations are those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $e_u:R\to u_*u^{-1}R$ be the unit of the sheafified-left-Kan-extension adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and put $\eta^\beta=u_*\beta\circ e_u$.

For every $T\to B$ in $B_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $a\in R(T)$, with $T\times_BV$ viewed over $V$ by the second projection, one has
$$e_{u,T}(a)=R(\operatorname{pr}_T)(a),\qquad \eta^\beta_T(a)=\bar\beta_{T\times_BV}\bigl(R(\operatorname{pr}_T)(a)\bigr),$$
where the first equality uses the stated restriction identification. For every $U\to V$ in $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and every $B$-map $b:U\to T$, let $\gamma_b=(b,U\to V):U\to T\times_BV$. Then
$$S(\gamma_b)\eta^\beta_T(a)=\bar\beta_U(R(b)(a)).$$
In particular, with $\delta:V\to V\times_BV$ the diagonal, the map $S(\delta)\eta^\beta_V$ is the ring isomorphism $\bar\beta_{V/V}:R(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(V,S)$. For a global section $r\in\Gamma(B,R)$, pullback of the map $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to R$ sending $1$ to $r$, followed by $\beta$, is the global section $\bar\beta_{V/V}(R(u)(r))$; the monoidal-unit comparison is the canonical one for inverse image.

proof.text: Write $L_p=u_{u,p}$ and let $j_{T,\phi}:R(T)\to L_pR(W)$ denote the Kan coprojection for $(T,\phi:W\to T\times_BV)$. The presheaf adjunction sends $t:L_pR\to H$ to $\alpha_T=t_{T\times_BV}j_{T,\mathrm{id}}$. Its inverse sends $\alpha:R\to u_*H$ to the map $j_{T,\phi}(a)\mapsto H(\phi)(\alpha_T(a))$. The latter respects the cocone relations by naturality of $\alpha$, and the two formulas are inverse by naturality of $t$. Taking $t$ to be the identity, then composing with the sheafification unit, shows that the specified sheaf adjunction unit $e_{u,T}$ is $j_{T,\mathrm{id}}$ followed by sheafification. This computes the composite adjunction in the cited statement, rather than choosing a different adjunction on an isomorphic functor. The inverse image $u^{-1}$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] used for the domain of $\beta$ is the same functor: it is the left Kan extension along the opposite of the same base-change functor $T\mapsto T\times_BV$, followed by sheafification, and we take that Kan extension by the pointwise colimit formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] (the two chosen product orders differ by the canonical swap, which induces an isomorphism of the indexing categories $\mathcal I_W$). Hence $u_*\beta\circ e_u$ is defined, and its ring-object version is the one obtained by applying this functor to the ring structure maps.

source.place: Tags 00VE (lemma-adjoints-u, explicit forward and inverse maps) and 00WX (lemma-adjoint-sheaves).

proof.text: Fix $T$ and put $W=T\times_BV$, $p=\operatorname{pr}_T$ and $v=\operatorname{pr}_V$. The distinguished initial index for $W/V$ in clause (1) of the restriction lemma is $q=(W,\gamma)$, where $\gamma=(\mathrm{id}_W,v):W\to W\times_BV$; use the canonical swap if the chosen base-change product has the opposite order. The arrow $p:W\to T$ is a morphism $q\to (T,\mathrm{id}_W)$ of $\mathcal I_W$, since $(p\times_B\mathrm{id}_V)\gamma=\mathrm{id}_W$. The colimit cocone relation is therefore $j_{T,\mathrm{id}}(a)=j_{W,\gamma}(R(p)(a))$. By clause (1), $j_{W,\gamma}$ followed by sheafification is exactly the inverse of the stated restriction identification at $W/V$. Thus that identification sends $e_{u,T}(a)$ to $R(p)(a)$. It also respects ring operations by the ring clause of the same statement.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), product adjunction; the distinguished coprojections in clause (1) of lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction.

proof.text:
Direct image evaluates a sheaf map at $T\times_BV$, by its definition. Hence the definition $\eta^\beta=u_*\beta\circ e_u$ and Step 2 give $\eta^\beta_T(a)=\bar\beta_{T\times_BV}(R(\operatorname{pr}_T)(a))$. For $U/V$ and the stated $B$-map $b:U\to T$, the pair $\gamma_b=(b,U\to V)$ is a morphism over $V$. Naturality of the sheaf map $\bar\beta:R|_V\to S$ and functoriality of restriction give
$$S(\gamma_b)\eta^\beta_T(a)=\bar\beta_U\bigl(R(\gamma_b)R(\operatorname{pr}_T)(a)\bigr)=\bar\beta_U(R(b)(a)),$$
since $\operatorname{pr}_T\gamma_b=b$. The restrictions of $R|_V$ are precisely those of $R$.

source.place: Tag 00Y0 (definition-localize), restriction formula following the definition; naturality applied to the graph.

proof.text: Set $T=V$, $U=V/V$ and $b=\mathrm{id}_V$ in Step 3. Then $\gamma_b=\delta$ and $R(b)=\mathrm{id}$, so $S(\delta)\eta^\beta_V=\bar\beta_{V/V}$. The object $V/V$ is terminal in $V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$: the only arrow to it from $U/V$ is the structure arrow. Thus evaluation there is $\Gamma(V,S)$. A sheaf isomorphism of rings has inverse components given by its inverse sheaf map, so $\bar\beta_{V/V}$ is the asserted ring isomorphism. No claim that $S(\delta)$ itself is invertible is needed.

source.place: Tag 00Y0 (definition-localize), category over V and sectionwise restriction.

proof.text: Let $z_r:\underline{\mathbf Z}_B\to R$ be the additive sheaf map with $z_r(1)=r$ at $B/B$. Naturality along $u$ gives $(z_r)_V(1)=R(u)(r)$. Clause (1) of the restriction lemma identifies $u^{-1}z_r$ with the restriction of $z_r$, so its value on the restricted constant section $1$ at $V/V$ is $R(u)(r)$. For the source of this map use clause (2) of that lemma with $A=\mathbf Z$: the coefficient isomorphism $c^u_{\mathbf Z}:u^{-1}\underline{\mathbf Z}_B\to\underline{\mathbf Z}_V$ identifies the restricted constant section $1$ with $1$. The canonical monoidal-unit map $\underline{\mathbf Z}_V\to u^{-1}\underline{\mathbf Z}_B$ is its inverse: in the canonical inverse-image tensor structure it is the unital map from the integer ring object, hence it sends $1$ to the pulled-back $1$. Under restriction these two maps are inverse since both preserve every integer section, and constant sheaf sections locally are integer sections. Therefore $\beta\circ u^{-1}z_r$, with this unit comparison, has global value $\bar\beta_{V/V}(R(u)(r))$, as required.
